_metadata.independence: I read only x12-rc-input.json (and re-read my own output to validate it); no other repository file, search, web or paid API was used.

hints.reason: ANGEL via the halo angels are drawn with; VIDEO GAME via the Halo series, a clean double meaning with a nice click.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent pair; HALO is the obvious and right hint.

hints.reason: BAND via the Eagles of Hotel California; BIRD via the bird of prey; classic rock is fine for a U.S. audience.

pairs.pair_note: Solid and fair; text is accurate.

hints.reason: BAND via The Who; DOCTOR via Doctor Who; both names are instantly familiar and the pairing is a satisfying click, so this phrase-join earns its pass.
hints.fix: Doctor Who is the classic TV show about a time traveler called the Doctor.

pairs.pair_note: Good phrase-join. The DOCTOR line (and explanation) calls Doctor Who the time traveller; the character is 'the Doctor', and U.S. spelling is 'traveler'. Minor polish only.

hints.reason: BAND via 'rubber band'; ELASTIC via rubber's defining stretchiness; easy and flat but fair and unambiguous.

pairs.pair_note: Low delight (the pair itself nearly spells 'elastic band'), but it is a clean, fair easy clue. The BAND line 'A rubber band.' is terse; something like 'A rubber band is a stretchy loop.' would read better.

hints.reason: BAND via 'rock band' is fine, but GARAGE depends on the genre name 'garage rock', which is less instantly familiar, and the pairing has no real payoff.
hints.fix: Garage rock is raw rock music named after bands that practiced in garages.

pairs.pair_note: The GARAGE line 'Garage rock is made in a garage' turns the genre name into a literal claim. No clearly better one-word hint found; ROCK is serviceable but unremarkable.

hints.reason: BAND via marching bands in a parade; MARCH via marching down the street in a parade; a clear, vivid scene.

pairs.pair_note: Clean scene clue; St. Patrick's Day parades in March are a small bonus reading.

hints.reason: ROAD via 'Abbey Road'; BAND via Abbey Road being the Beatles album with the famous crossing cover, an indirect but well-known aha.

pairs.pair_note: BAND side is one step indirect (Abbey Road -> Beatles -> band), which is the satisfying kind. Lines are accurate.

hints.reason: BAND via The Police of 'Every Breath You Take'; THIEF via the police catching thieves; a crisp double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; the band reading is a pleasant twist on an obvious association.

hints.reason: BAND via ring being a synonym of band in the jewelry sense, and WEDDING via 'wedding ring'; both sides use the same sense, so the hint just restates the compound 'wedding band' with a synonym rather than linking two ideas.

pairs.pair_note: Judgement call: it is easy and works, but it is a synonym restatement rather than a double meaning. A hint using the music sense of band (for example RECEPTION, where the band plays) would be a real link, though not clearly great.

hints.reason: BASEBALL via the batter at the plate; CAKE via cake batter; a classic, clean double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: DRIVER-style double meaning; excellent.

hints.reason: BASEBALL via a base hit; MUSIC via a hit song; a clear double meaning even though other words could fit one side.

pairs.pair_note: Simple and fair. The explanation is a fragment; 'A hit is a popular song, and a batter gets a hit in baseball.' would read better.

hints.reason: BASKETBALL via the slam dunk; COOKIE via dunking a cookie in milk; a fun, vivid double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent and playful.

hints.reason: BEEF via steak as a cut of beef; VAMPIRE only via the homophone 'stake', a well-known groaner pun that the explanation states honestly.

pairs.pair_note: Judgement call: the vampire side works by sound, not spelling, and players see only the written word. The steak/stake pun is familiar and satisfying, and no better hint exists for this pair, so I lean PASS.

hints.reason: BOOK via 'bookworm'; FISHING via worms as bait; instantly familiar on both sides.

pairs.pair_note: Clean, easy and pleasant.

hints.reason: BOXING via the championship title belt; PANTS via the belt that holds them up; a clear double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Solid; 'below the belt' adds a little extra boxing flavour.

hints.reason: CANDY via Nerds candy; GENIUS via nerds as the brainy type, a slight stretch from nerd to genius but an easy one.

pairs.pair_note: SMARTIES (candy / 'smarty') is an equally good alternative; neither is clearly better. The GENIUS line slightly overstates ('A nerd is a brainy genius type'); 'Nerds are known as brainy types.' would be more precise.

hints.reason: CARD via the joker in a deck; CLOWN via joker as a jester/clown, reinforced by Batman's clown villain.

pairs.pair_note: Strong and obvious in the good way.

hints.reason: CARD via the spades suit; SHOVEL via a spade being a digging tool; a classic double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Fine; lines are accurate (a spade is a type of shovel).

hints.reason: CAT via the Grumpy Cat meme; DWARF via Grumpy of Snow White's seven dwarfs; two famous Grumpies make a real 'oh, nice'.
hints.fix: Grumpy Cat was a famous internet cat.

pairs.pair_note: One of the best in the batch. Grumpy Cat died in 2019, so the CAT line should be past tense.

hints.reason: CEREAL via Lucky Charms; LEPRECHAUN via Lucky the Leprechaun mascot and the luck-of-the-Irish association; a familiar cereal-mascot reference.
hints.fix: Lucky the Leprechaun is the Lucky Charms mascot.

pairs.pair_note: Strong. The LEPRECHAUN line starts with 'Its', which is unclear when the line is read on its own.

hints.reason: CHOCOLATE via Hershey's the chocolate maker; KISS via Hershey's Kisses; an instantly familiar brand link.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, fair brand clue.

hints.reason: CHURCH via a temple as a place of worship; HEAD via the temple at the side of the head; a satisfying double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Good; the text correctly says 'place of worship' rather than claiming a temple is a church.

hints.reason: COMPUTER via a software bug; INSECT via bug as an everyday word for an insect; the two senses are genuinely distinct, so it reads as a double meaning rather than a restatement.

pairs.pair_note: Judgement call: BUG is close to a colloquial synonym of INSECT, but unlike RING/WEDDING the other side uses a separate sense, so I pass it as a classic double meaning.

hints.reason: DANCE via a ball as a formal dance; NEW YEAR via the Times Square ball drop; a nice double meaning with a vivid image.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; accurate text.

hints.reason: DISNEY via Mickey's dog Pluto; PLANET via Pluto the former ninth planet; the text handles the demotion correctly.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent; one of the best in the batch.

hints.reason: DOG via Snoopy, Charlie Brown's beagle; PILOT via his famous World War I Flying Ace routine against the Red Baron, familiar Peanuts knowledge with a real aha.

pairs.pair_note: The PILOT side is one step indirect but well known (doghouse-as-plane, Red Baron).

hints.reason: DUCK via 'duck hunt'; VIDEO GAME only through that same phrase as the classic NES Duck Hunt, which is iconic enough (light gun, laughing dog) to click for most U.S. players.

pairs.pair_note: Judgement call: HUNT reaches VIDEO GAME only via the title 'Duck Hunt', so both sides rest on one phrase. The title is famous, so I pass it, but younger players may miss the game side.

hints.reason: EYE via 'eyelid'; JAR via a jar lid; instantly familiar on both sides with a neat 'both are covers' symmetry.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, clean, pleasant.

hints.reason: FISH via bass the fish; GUITAR via the bass guitar; a classic double meaning (and heteronym).

pairs.pair_note: Classic. The explanation 'A bass is a fish and a guitar' is slightly loose; the lines are accurate.

hints.reason: FOOTBALL via the Indianapolis Colts; HORSE via a colt being a young (male) horse; a fair sports-team double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: BRONCO (Denver Broncos) would be an equally good alternative; neither is clearly better.

hints.reason: FRUIT via the date fruit; VALENTINE via a Valentine's date; a crisp double meaning with a nice switch.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent; the VALENTINE line 'A Valentine's date.' is terse but true.

hints.reason: GUM via Trident gum; SEA via the trident of the sea god Poseidon/Neptune (and King Triton); a satisfying brand-plus-myth link.

pairs.pair_note: One of the best in the batch; text is accurate.

hints.reason: HAM via Spam, the canned pork-and-ham meat; MAIL via spam as junk email; a great double meaning.
hints.fix: Spam is canned pork made with ham.

pairs.pair_note: Strong idea, but 'Spam is canned ham' (line and explanation) is inaccurate: Spam is canned pork with ham, not canned ham. The explanation should also say 'junk email' rather than 'junk mail'.

hints.reason: LINK via the hero of The Legend of Zelda; VIDEO GAME via the Zelda series itself; plays nicely on the famous Link-is-not-Zelda mix-up.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent; text is accurate.

hints.reason: MARVEL via Thor the Avenger; THUNDER via Thor the Norse god of thunder; easy and fully accurate.

pairs.pair_note: Obvious but clean and satisfying.

hints.reason: MUSIC via a film or musical score; SOCCER via scoring a goal; a clear double meaning (other sports fitting is not a reason to fail).

pairs.pair_note: Solid DRIVER-style double meaning.

hints.reason: PEACE via the dove as a peace symbol; SOAP via the Dove bar brand; a satisfying symbol-plus-brand double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Strong. (Dove markets its bar as a 'beauty bar', but 'soap brand' is the everyday understanding and is fine.)

hints.reason: VIDEO GAME via Angry Birds; PIG via the green pigs the birds are flung at, familiar indirect knowledge with a real aha.

pairs.pair_note: PIG side is one step indirect (Angry Birds -> green pigs), but Angry Birds is ubiquitous; satisfying.

hints.reason: VIDEO GAME via the Pokémon series; POCKET via the true fact that Pokémon is short for 'Pocket Monsters', a widely circulated piece of trivia that gives a good aha once explained.

pairs.pair_note: Judgement call: the POCKET side depends on knowing 'Pocket Monsters'. Fans and many casual players know it; others will get it only from the explanation. Could be BORDERLINE under a stricter read.

hints.reason: RACE via go-kart racing; VIDEO GAME via Mario Kart; both sides stand on their own and Mario Kart is iconic.

pairs.pair_note: Clean and fair.

hints.reason: TENT via pitching a tent; SOCCER via the pitch as the field, a British-origin term now common in U.S. soccer coverage; the baseball misdirection makes the switch satisfying.

pairs.pair_note: Judgement call: 'pitch' for a soccer field leans British, but U.S. World Cup and MLS coverage uses it widely. The SOCCER line could read 'In soccer, the field is often called the pitch.'

hints.reason: TENNIS via 'love' meaning zero; VALENTINE via Valentine's Day love; a well-known and charming double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent; accurate text.
